claims.text: The initial CrMnFeCoNi alloy is equiatomic.
Homogenization produces a homogeneous FCC matrix in equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
Aging homogenized equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi at 600–700°C for 2–4 hours induces a B2-ordered secondary phase.
The proposed aging treatment produces fine, uniformly dispersed B2 precipitates within the FCC matrix.
Fine B2 precipitates impede dislocation motion through Orowan strengthening.
B2 precipitate/FCC matrix interfaces initiate transformation-induced plasticity.
Orowan strengthening and interface-induced transformation plasticity jointly increase yield strength, ductility, and fracture toughness.
Phase-homogenization effects associated with the treatment help tailor Young’s modulus.
The treatment will increase yield strength by more than 20% relative to the conventional homogenized FCC state.
The treatment will increase elongation relative to a conventionally processed single-FCC baseline.
The treatment will increase fracture toughness relative to a conventionally processed single-FCC baseline.
An inert atmosphere is required to avoid oxidation during aging.
Maintaining the specified aging temperature and time prevents precipitate coarsening.
Over-aging can cause precipitate coarsening and eliminate the proposed property improvements.
Formation of unintended intermetallic phases can cause embrittlement.
The quantitative mechanical-property improvements depend on attaining an optimal precipitate size and distribution.

contradictions.description: Over-aging and precipitate coarsening are presented as conditions outside the hypothesis's expected domain, but coarsening-induced embrittlement is also treated as a decisive falsification. A failed specimen outside the stated valid processing window would test the boundary condition rather than necessarily falsify the in-domain hypothesis.
